subject: Electrical Engineering
title: Grid-Tied Inverters: Feeding the Grid
description: A micro-lesson that makes Grid-Tied Inverters: Feeding the Grid usable.

hook.text: A grid-tied inverter synchronizes its AC output with the utility grid — matching voltage, frequency, and phase.

buildup.text: A phase-locked loop (PLL) tracks the grid's voltage waveform and locks the inverter's output to it.

discovery.text: Current control ensures power flows from the inverter to the grid — not the other way around.

twist.text: Anti-islanding protection disconnects the inverter if the grid goes down — preventing electrocution of line workers.

climax.text: Every rooftop solar panel system uses a grid-tied inverter to sell excess energy back to the utility.

punchline.text: Sync, inject, protect — grid-tied inverters turn rooftops into power plants.

quiz.question: Why is anti-islanding protection required in grid-tied inverters?
options: To prevent the inverter from drawing power from the grid at night
To disconnect during grid outages so line workers aren't exposed to live voltage
To reduce power output during peak demand hours
